structured.approach: Attempt 2 fixes the G3 refusal. One claim quoted story labels I assigned in this step (for example "STORY-06"). The check read their digits as numbers, and they do not appear in feat.trd or feat.prd. In this result, every claim describes a story by its function (the paid_date story, the serialiser story and so on). Every remaining digit in a claim comes from the source it cites. I rewrote feat.stories in full. Its story content is the attempt-1 version after the verifier's corrections. It now also has a note saying the EP/FT/STORY/TK/AC-nn.n/SA/SQ labels are assigned in this step, a revision note for attempt 2, and one fix in the carried open-items map: OQ-B6 now also lists the delay-history story. The method is the same as attempt 1. I read the four contracted inputs, the existing unit test files and predict.py. I split the work into one epic, five features (one per lane), eight NEW stories and their tasks, following the story template. Each story gives frame links to the prototype's text frames, dependencies, a specification depth, and [Pending] markers on criteria that rest on open questions. No priority is set. A verifier pass on attempt 1 found 11 issues, and all of them are fixed in this content.

claims.text: The story template requires ID, title, As a/I want/So that, acceptance criteria in Gherkin (Given/When/Then), assumptions and open items; every story in feat.stories follows it.
The work is split into one feature per lane: ap_pipeline to Data Engineering, ap_forecast to Data Science, ap_aging to Backend, ap_portal to Frontend, and the end-to-end story to the Testing Agent.
The stories cover PRD acceptance criteria AC-1 to AC-23 and user stories US-1 to US-5, with no scope beyond S-1 to S-7.
Every TRD test T-1 to T-17 maps to at least one story acceptance criterion.
The delay-history story depends on the paid_date feed story, because delays_by_vendor reads the paid_date key that the feed change adds to each record.

The JSON serialiser story depends on the overdue-list story. The portal table story depends only on the CT-1 contract. The end-to-end story depends on the feed, delay-history, risk, overdue-list, serialiser and portal stories.
There are two external dependencies: feed v3 availability (PQ-6) for the paid_date story, and the order relative to PROV-ACME-2026-11 (PQ-5) for the explanation story.
An unpaid invoice exactly 30 days past due is not listed, and one 31 days past due is listed, as in prototype rows SYN-INV-005 and SYN-INV-001.
vendor_risk returns 'medium' for a predicted delay of exactly 30 and 'low' for exactly 10. predict_delay_days is a rounded mean that counts negative delays as 0 and returns 0 for an empty history.
Amounts stay Decimal quantised to two decimals in ap_aging and travel as two-decimal strings in CT-1 (for example "1250.00"). ap_portal never formats them through a float.
Frame links point to the prototype's text frames SC-1, WF-1, WF-2 and flows 4.1 and 4.2, because Figma is not connected (PQ-P6).
Each lane keeps CI green with coverage of at least 90%. The Python repositories use Python 3.9 and ap_portal uses Node.js 22.
New unit tests go into the existing test files tests/test_pipeline.py, tests/test_forecast.py and tests/test_aging.py.
All stories are in NEW state, and no priority, iteration or estimate is set.
No conflict with D-2026-031, D-2026-044 or D-2026-050 was found. The difference between the prototype and the TRD on padding a one-decimal amount is already raised as TQ-11 and is kept pending.

open_questions: Priority, iteration and estimates for the stories are not set. Backlog prioritisation is for the PM.
Should TQ-1 (bucket_for(30) returns "31-60") and TQ-2 (formatAmount formats through a float) become separate NEW items? They are out of scope here, so no story was written for them.
The TRD was approved, but no input records answers to TQ-1 to TQ-11. Were any answered at the REQ-07 gate, in particular TQ-3 (approval of CT-1)? Answers would lift the [Pending] markers.

Definition of ready: must the pending items (OQ-B6, OQ-B8, OQ-B9, OQ-B10, PQ-1, PQ-2, PQ-5, PQ-P7, TQ-3 to TQ-11) be answered before stories enter an iteration, or may the lanes start on the interim designs?
Carried unchanged: OQ-B1 to OQ-B10, PQ-1 to PQ-6, PQ-P1 to PQ-P7, TQ-1 to TQ-11, FQ-3/FQ-5/FQ-6, OQ-1 to OQ-5 and Q-1 to Q-5. Section 6.2 of feat.stories maps each one to the stories it affects.
structured.summary: I rewrote feat.stories in full for attempt 2. It holds one epic, five features (one per lane), eight NEW stories and their tasks. Every story has numbered Gherkin acceptance criteria, PRD and TRD traces, links to the prototype's text frames, dependencies, a specification depth, assumptions and open items. Every PRD criterion and every TRD test maps to a story. Criteria that rest on open questions are marked [Pending]. To fix the G3 refusal, the claims now describe stories by their function instead of by labels assigned in this step, and the file says those labels are its own. No conflict was found with the decision log or any approved output. Nothing is blocking.
